prompt: The lesson’s exponential attack aims at 1.2 but switches to decay when the level reaches 1.0. Why aim beyond the switching level?

options.text: To make the output deliberately exceed full scale
options.explanation: The code clamps at the peak and switches stage; the target does not become the output peak.

options.text: To make attack duration equal the time constant automatically
options.explanation: The duration also depends on the starting level, target and stopping level.

options.text: Because exponential curves cannot change from zero
options.explanation: A positive target produces a non-zero first step from zero.

options.text: So the curve crosses the peak in finite time instead of approaching it indefinitely
options.explanation: Correct. A target beyond the transition threshold gives the state machine a reachable end condition.

workedExample: If the target were exactly the peak, ideal remaining-gap updates would approach it without arriving. A target above the peak lets the trajectory cross the threshold. At that crossing, clamp to the intended peak and move to decay.
